VILLANUEVA BACKS PROBE INTO TOP FLOOD CONTROL CONTRACTORS

Senate Majority Leader Joel Villanueva welcomed President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.'s call to investigate the 15 contractors with the most flood control projects, saying it vindicates his long-standing concerns over alleged irregularities in the Department of Public Works and Highways' (DPWH) ₱1–₱1.4 billion daily flood control budget.

Villanueva, who has raised the issue since 2023, denied any Senate link to the firms named by the President and urged authorities to ensure accountability. He said he has requested the Securities and Exchange Commission to release the companies' General Information Sheets and Articles of Incorporation to aid in verifying connections.

While leaving it to the President to decide whether DPWH Secretary Manuel Bonoan should step aside during the probe, Villanueva stressed the need for an impartial investigation and a truly integrated flood control plan. He also welcomed San Miguel Corp. President Ramon Ang's offer to address Metro Manila flooding at no cost to the government, provided it aligns with the national master plan.
